transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, the desiccant replacement on the central compressed-air dryer for Lines 5 and 7 is due this week. Before I finalize the work order and set the shutdown window, we need to run through the standard pre-shutdown review. I'd like to hear from quality, utilities, production control, and EHS so we can coordinate timing and make sure the portable compressor is staged correctly. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a quality concern before we finalize this. My quality review found that Line 7's pneumatic process requires compressed air at a dew point of -40 degrees Celsius or lower. The portable compressor that's been staged for temporary service during the dryer work cannot meet that dew point limit. I recorded this requirement in today's quality notebook but haven't yet attached it to the shutdown work order, so I want to make sure everyone is aware now before the work order is finalized.

transcript.text: I have important timing information for this shutdown. I confirmed with the dryer service technician this morning by email: the desiccant replacement requires 5 hours of isolation work, followed by exactly 2 hours of pressure stabilization before production air can be released. That's a total of 7 hours before Lines 5 and 7 can resume normal production air service. This estimate hasn't been entered into the maintenance schedule yet, so we need to account for it when finalizing the shutdown window.
